content:
World Athletics has announced the 20 nominees for the 2026 World Athlete of the Year awards, and Masai Russell of the United States leads the women's field after one of the most dominant hurdling seasons in history. The three finalists in each category will be announced November 10 and 11, with the winners crowned at the World Athletics Awards in Monaco on November 29.

Russell, the Paris Olympic champion in the 100-meter hurdles, went unbeaten in all 14 of her races in 2026. She set a world record of 12.09 seconds at the Diamond League meeting in Zurich in August, breaking Tobi Amusan's previous mark, and recorded nine of the 10 fastest times of the season. She capped the year by winning both the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship and the Diamond League title, and she is now aiming for her first World Championships title in 2027 before defending her Olympic crown in Los Angeles in 2028.

The women's nominees are Tigst Assefa of Ethiopia, Chase Jackson of the United States, Melissa Jefferson-Wooden of the United States, Agnes Ngetich of Kenya, Marileidy Paulino of the Dominican Republic, Maria Perez of Spain, Camryn Rogers of Canada, Masai Russell of the United States, Audrey Werro of Switzerland, and Yan Ziyi of China. The men's nominees are Kenneth Bednarek of the United States, Kristjan Ceh of Slovenia, Andy Diaz Hernandez of Italy, Alison dos Santos of Brazil, Mondo Duplantis of Sweden, Collen Kebinatshipi of Botswana, Josh Kerr of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage of Sri Lanka, Sabastian Sawe of Kenya, and Ja'Kobe Tharp of the United States.

World records fell across the sport in 2026. Assefa won the Berlin Marathon in 2:11:04, the third-fastest time in history, after winning London with a women-only world record of 2:15:41. Ngetich set a world record in the women's half marathon and Perez set the inaugural half-marathon race walk record. On the men's side, world records came from dos Santos in the 400-meter hurdles, Duplantis in the pole vault, Kerr in the mile, Sawe in the marathon, and Tharp in the 110-meter hurdles.

This year the awards carry a new format, with a single women's and a single men's World Athlete of the Year honor instead of separate track, field, and out-of-stadium categories. The winner is decided by a four-way vote, with athletes, media, the World Athletics Family, and fans each holding a 25 percent share. Voting closed October 17.

The road to Los Angeles 2028 is already taking shape. World Athletics announced the marathon qualification process for LA28, with the eligibility period running from November 1, 2026, to April 30, 2028, and 70 quota places for each gender. Entry standards will be published in December. Duplantis, meanwhile, will skip the 2027 indoor season to focus on training and recovery ahead of the outdoor season and the World Championships in Beijing in mid-September.

Off the track, the race to succeed Sebastian Coe as president of World Athletics is underway. Coe steps down next year after leading the federation since 2015, and four candidates have entered the race: Raul Chapado of Spain, Antti Pihlakoski of Finland, Ximena Restrepo of Colombia, and Adille Sumariwalla of India. The winner will be announced on the eve of the 2027 World Championships in Beijing.

This weekend, the athletics program at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opens Sunday and runs through Tuesday, the 43rd Athens Authentic Marathon runs Sunday on the original course from Marathon to Athens, and five Kenyans line up at the Cross Internacional de Italica in Seville, Spain.

Sources: World Athletics; NBC Sports; FloTrack; Track & Field News; BlackNews.com.
